direction1.title: [Bug]: WhatsApp outbound media silently dropped — hasMedia: false — CLI and model-initiated sends affected (v2026.4.8–4.9)
direction1.author: AllenKWPaley
direction1.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

All WhatsApp outbound media fails silently regardless of trigger path — CLI --media flag and model-initiated sends are both affected. The model may attempt and "confirm" media delivery repeatedly without any indication of failure, burning tokens and misleading the user.

### Steps to reproduce

We traced the full media path through the minified dist. The call chain breaks down as follows:

Media enters session processing and is saved to disk via persistChatSendImages → returns savedImages with filesystem paths (server.impl-BxLfE9ri.js:12837)
resolveChatSendTranscriptMediaFields stores those paths as MediaPath/MediaPaths in the transcript only (server.impl-BxLfE9ri.js:12873)
reply-BwK-bN2w.js:1696-1697 reads MediaPaths — but exclusively to inject a [media attached] text note into the LLM prompt. No path→URL conversion occurs here.
resolveSendableOutboundReplyParts (reply-payload-CcbNO0Ax.js:65-68) assembles the outbound payload — mediaUrls is empty because nothing bridged the saved filesystem paths into it
WhatsApp sender evaluates hasMedia: Boolean(options.mediaUrl) → false
Message is delivered as text only. No error is raised.

Confirmed no path→URL conversion mechanism exists in the reply pipeline:
bashgrep -n "pathToUrl\|fileToUrl\|gatewayUrl\|serveFile" reply-BwK-bN2w.js
# returns nothing

### Expected behavior

ogg audio file passed to user handset in WhatsApp to be playable

### Actual behavior

Silent failure,  "..." other party is typing dots appear, no message comes through.

v2026.4.8–4.9

### Operating system

Mint 22

Official one-liner install script

ChatGPT5.4 Codex

direction1.title: chat.history leaks system-level memory injection blocks to WebChat UI
direction1.author: JackChen201535
direction1.body:
## Describe the bug

The WebChat UI (macOS native app, Control UI) renders system-level memory injection blocks that should be invisible to users. These blocks contain internal prompts like:

```
## Memory system — ACTION REQUIRED

Auto-recall found no relevant results for a long query. You MUST call `memory_search` now with a shortened query (2-5 key words) before answering. Do not skip this step. Do NOT answer without searching first.
```

and

```
Read HEARTBEAT.md if it exists (workspace context). Follow it strictly. Do not infer or repeat old tasks from prior chats. If nothing needs attention, reply HEARTBEAT_OK.
When reading HEARTBEAT.md, use workspace file /Users/jackchen/.openclaw/workspace/HEARTBEAT.md (exact case). Do not read docs/heartbeat.md.
```

## Expected behavior

These are internal system prompts injected for the agent, not user-facing content. The `chat.history` response should strip them before rendering to the UI.

The docs mention that `chat.history` strips inline delivery directives (`[[reply_to_*]]`), `NO_REPLY`, and tool-call XML, but memory/heartbeat system injection blocks are not currently filtered.

## To reproduce

1. Start a fresh session
2. When auto-recall finds no relevant results, the system injects the memory search prompt
3. The prompt appears visible in the WebChat UI

## Environment

- **OpenClaw version:** 2026.4.9 (0512059)
- **Platform:** macOS (arm64)
- **Memory plugin:** memos-local-openclaw-plugin
- **Channel:** webchat (Control UI)

## Suggested fix

Add filtering in `chat.history` for system injection blocks. These typically appear as:
- `## Memory system — ACTION REQUIRED` blocks
- Heartbeat prompt blocks (starting with `Read HEARTBEAT.md`)

Similar to how `[[reply_to_*]]` and `NO_REPLY` are already stripped.

direction1.title: [Bug]: Control UI webchat re-injects assistant responses as new user input (hybrid mirror routing bug)
direction1.author: cobra281
direction1.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

# [Bug]: Control UI webchat re-injects assistant responses as new user input (hybrid mirror routing bug)

## Description

When external messages (e.g., iMessage) are mirrored into the Control UI webchat session, the assistant's outbound responses are being re-injected back into the same session as new user messages, creating an infinite echo loop.

## Environment

- OpenClaw version: 2026.4.9
- Gateway mode: local (port 18789)
- Channel: iMessage (mirrored into Control UI webchat)
- Session: agent:main:main (direct messages)
- Reproduce environment: macOS M4 Pro

## Root Cause Analysis

This appears to be a hybrid combination of:
- **Issue #5964** (Control UI duplicate messages): Client-side rendering may re-render chat events
- **Control UI session routing bug**: Outbound assistant messages aren't marked as "internal" or "already-sent" before being fed back into chat.inject or the session history fetch
- **Missing deduplication**: Unlike issue #1649 (iMessage self-chat), there's no logic to detect that a message came from the agent itself

---

**Severity:** High (causes infinite loops in automation)  
**Type:** Session routing / Control UI webchat bug

**Labels to add:** `bug`, `control-ui`, `webchat`, `routing`

### Steps to reproduce

## Reproduction Steps

1. Have an agent receive a message from an external channel (e.g., iMessage from a user contact)
2. Message is mirrored into the Control UI webchat as a user message (delivery-mirror)
3. Agent responds (e.g., "Yep, same conclusion — GPT-5.4")
4. Agent's response is re-injected back into the webchat as a new user message
5. Agent processes it again, creating a feedback loop

direction1.title: [Bug]: Inbound reaction context events arrive but do not trigger an agent turn (Telegram)
direction1.author: M-Lietz
direction1.body:
## Environment
- OpenClaw v2026.4.10 (44e5b62)
- Node.js v22.22.1
- Telegram (long-polling), grammY
- Config: `messages.reactions.level: "extensive"`, `messages.reactions.triggerAgentTurn: true`

## Description

When a user reacts to a message in Telegram (e.g. adds a 👍 or ❤️ emoji), the gateway receives the `message_reaction` update and logs it as a context event, but **no agent turn is triggered** in response.

### Observed behavior

1. User adds reaction to a message → Telegram sends `message_reaction` update
2. Gateway receives and logs the event as an inbound context event
3. **No agent run starts** — the reaction is recorded in session context but the agent never processes it
4. If the user sends a text message afterwards, the agent can see the reaction in its context history

### Expected behavior

With `triggerAgentTurn: true`, inbound reactions should wake the agent for a turn, allowing it to respond to the reaction (e.g. acknowledge it, respond contextually).

### Additional context

- Hot-reload of config does not seem to fix this — a full gateway restart was required during testing
- The feature may never have worked end-to-end (unclear if this is a regression or an incomplete feature)
- This affects both DM and group contexts

## Reproduction

1. Configure `messages.reactions.level: "extensive"` and `messages.reactions.triggerAgentTurn: true`
2. Send a message in Telegram DM with the bot
3. React to one of the bot's messages with any emoji
4. Observe: no agent turn starts, reaction is only recorded as context event

direction1.title: [Bug]: imessage echo loop
direction1.author: fagandesign
direction1.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

iMessage reflects assistant outbound text back as inbound user messages in direct chat, causing loops.

### Steps to reproduce

1. send message to agent in imessage.
2. agent sends message back
3. agent receives its own message back
4. agent keeps replying to its own messages
5. eventually agent stops replying to self, but echo persists


### Expected behavior

expected behavior is that the agent would not see its own message returned. there would be a smooth conversation with no filtering required. 

### Actual behavior

Evidence:
1) Session metadata shows self-addressed route:
   ~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json
   origin.from == origin.to == imessage:+xxxxxxxxxx

2) In session log, assistant messages are re-ingested as user content with control-char prefixes (e.g. ��\^@):
   ~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/6b18f336-84ff-4525-9736-32eaece59b25.jsonl

3) Runtime decision path:
   /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/monitor-provider-ClqFz1Hj.js
   function resolveIMessageInboundDecision()
   around line ~917 (params.message.is_from_me branch)

Root cause:
For self-chat-shaped routing, is_from_me messages could continue if echo-cache match missed, so reflected assistant text could dispatch as inbound.

Local hotfix that resolved it:
Force-drop all inbound is_from_me iMessage events (including self-chat) in resolveIMessageInboundDecision:

if (params.message.is_from_me) {
  params.selfChatCache?.remember(selfChatLookup);
  return { kind: "drop", reason: isSelfChat ? "from me self-chat" : "from me" };
}

Request:
Please patch upstream iMessage monitor so inbound is_from_me cannot dispatch, and harden reflection detection against control-char-prefixed refl

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Summary

**Title:** Control UI replies to Telegram-backed session are delivered to `webchat` instead of Telegram

**Summary**
When opening or interacting with a Telegram direct session from the OpenClaw Control UI, replies are delivered to `webchat` rather than being sent back to Telegram. Telegram transport itself works; explicit cross-session send works too. The issue appears to be reply routing / delivery context selection.

**Environment**
- OpenClaw: `2026.3.12 (6472949)`
- OS: macOS arm64
- Gateway: local, running
- Telegram channel: `ON / OK`
- Control UI: local dashboard

If I open a Telegram direct session in the Control UI and reply there, the reply should go back to the Telegram chat for that session.

**What actually happens**
- Messages sent from Telegram to OpenClaw are received correctly.
- Replies generated after a Telegram-originated message are delivered to Telegram correctly.
- But when I type from the **web UI / Control UI** while viewing that Telegram-backed session, the reply stays in **webchat** instead of being sent to Telegram.
- If I use an explicit `sessions_send` to the Telegram session, the message reaches Telegram.

**Repro steps**
1. Ensure Telegram channel is connected and working.
2. Send a message from Telegram to the bot/user session.
3. Open the corresponding Telegram direct session in the Control UI.
4. Send a message from the Control UI in that session.
5. Observe that the reply appears in web UI, but does not get delivered to Telegram.
6. Use explicit `sessions_send` to the Telegram session.
7. Observe that Telegram receives that message successfully.

**Observed evidence**
`openclaw status` showed Telegram connected and the direct Telegram session present

direction1.author: superfat1988
direction1.body:
## Summary

`openclaw@2026.4.10` appears to ship without the `qa/scenarios/*` files, but the CLI startup path still hard-depends on them through `qa-lab`.

As a result, unrelated commands like:

```bash
openclaw completion --write-state
```

can fail before the command itself runs.

## Version

- openclaw: `2026.4.10`

## Repro

Install:

```bash
npm i -g openclaw@2026.4.10
```

Then run:

```bash
openclaw completion --write-state
```

## Actual result

CLI fails during startup with errors like:

```text
Error: qa scenario pack not found: qa/scenarios/index.md
```

After adding a minimal `qa/scenarios/index.md`, startup then fails with:

```text
Error: unknown qa scenario: source-docs-discovery-report
```

## Expected result

`openclaw completion --write-state` should run successfully, and unrelated CLI commands should not be blocked by missing QA scenario-pack files.

## Evidence

The published package metadata for `openclaw@2026.4.10` does not include `qa/` in the `files` whitelist:


direction1.author: Theo-jobs
direction1.body:
## Summary

In OpenClaw `2026.4.5`, Telegram DM voice messages arrive as raw `<media:audio>` placeholders with no transcription attempt, despite `tools.media.audio` being correctly configured and the fix from #61008 being present in the dist.

## Environment

- **OpenClaw:** 2026.4.5 (3e72c03)
- **OS:** macOS (Darwin 25.4.0, arm64)
- **Channel:** Telegram DM
- **STT Provider:** Groq (whisper-large-v3) — loaded and verified working via direct API call
- **Gateway mode:** local

## Root cause (traced in dist)

The fix from #61008 correctly widened the preflight condition in `bot-message-context-ID6QScNo.js` line 121:

```js
if (hasAudio && !hasUserText && (!isGroup || requireMention && ...)) {
  preflightTranscript = await transcribeFirstAudio({ ctx: {
    MediaPaths: allMedia.length > 0 ? allMedia.map((m) => m.path) : void 0,
    MediaTypes: allMedia.length > 0 ? allMedia.map((m) => m.contentType).filter(Boolean) : void 0
  }, cfg, agentDir: void 0 });
}
```

However, `allMedia[n].path` is `undefined` for Telegram voice notes. This is confirmed in `bot-message-context-ID6QScNo.js` around lines 340–390, where `contextMedia` objects are built with:

```js
MediaPath: contextMedia.length > 0 ? contextMedia[0]?.path : void 0,
MediaPaths: contextMedia.length > 0 ? contextMedia.map((m) => m.path) : void 0,
```

When `contextMedia[n].path` is `undefined`, `normalizeAttachments()` in `runner-Bo7fJw79.js` filters out the entry:

```js
.filter((entry) => Boolean(entry.path?.trim() || entry.url?.trim()))
```

So `transcribeFirstAudio` receives an empty attachment list and returns immediately — no transcription, no error, no log (errors are caught and only emitted via `logVerbose`, which is `off` by default).

direction1.title: [Bug]: `heartbeat.model` config is ignored — heartbeat uses default/fallback model instead
direction1.author: sbmilburn
direction1.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary

The `agents.defaults.heartbeat.model` configuration setting is ignored. Heartbeat sessions use the agent's default model (or its fallback chain) instead of the explicitly configured heartbeat model. This makes it impossible to run heartbeats on a cheaper/free model tier.

## Version

- **OpenClaw:** `2026.3.1`
- **OS:** Ubuntu Linux 6.8.0-101-generic (x64)
- **Node:** v25.6.1
- **Channel:** WhatsApp



### Steps to reproduce


1. Configure `heartbeat.model` to a model different from the agent's primary model (e.g., a free-tier OpenRouter model) see snippet below. 
2. Set `heartbeat.every` to `"5m"` (or any short interval for testing)
3. Ensure `activeHours` covers the current time
4. Wait for heartbeat to fire
5. Check OpenRouter activity logs (or equivalent provider logs) for which model was actually called


## Configuration

Relevant section from `openclaw.json`:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "model": {
        "primary": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6",
        "fallbacks": [
          "openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6",
          "openrouter/meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free",
          "openrouter/anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5"
        ]
      },
      "heartbeat": {
        "every": "5m",
        "activeHours": {
          "start": "08:00",
          "end": "22:00",
          "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles"
        },
        "model": "openrouter/meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free",
        "directPolicy": "allow"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

direction1.title: [Bug]: (doctor): plugins.allow advisory doesn't warn it's an exclusive allowlist
direction1.author: BKF-Gitty
direction1.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

openclaw doctor advises adding a plugin to plugins.allow without warning that this field is an exclusive allowlist — all plugins not listed are disabled, causing silent breakage of active channels, memory, and integrations.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run openclaw doctor with a working setup (Discord, Telegram, memory-core, memory-wiki all active)
2. Doctor suggests adding lossless-claw to plugins.allow
3. Add plugins.allow: ["lossless-claw"] to openclaw.json as advised
4. Restart gateway
5. Discord, Telegram, memory-core, and memory-wiki all fail to load — only lossless-claw is active

Either: (a) doctor's advisory includes all currently-active plugins in the suggested plugins.allow value, or (b) doctor warns that plugins.allow is exclusive and unlisted plugins will be disabled, or (c) the plugin loader emits a warning at startup when plugins.allow would disable currently-active plugins.

### Actual behavior

Doctor suggests adding a single plugin to plugins.allow with no mention of exclusivity. Following the advice disables all other plugins. No warning at startup. 4-hour outage before root cause was identified by manually reviewing config changes.
